official.deadline_note: No central deadline exists: RTP scholarships are administered by individual eligible universities, each with its own application and selection process and its own deadlines. Prospective students must contact the chosen university's postgraduate research office directly.
official.status_note: Ongoing block-grant program with no central application round - the Department of Education does not accept applications; eligible universities run their own RTP scholarship application and selection processes, so check each target university for its current round.
official.tuition_coverage_note: RTP scholarships can include a tuition fees offset (RTP Fees Offset) to assist with the course fees that would otherwise be payable by a higher degree by research (HDR) student, awarded by the university for the duration of the candidature.
benefits: Tuition fees offset (RTP Fees Offset) for HDR course fees at an eligible Australian university.
A stipend for general living costs: 2026 full-time rates run from a base of $34,315 to a maximum of $53,608 per year; 2027 rates are $35,550 base to $55,537 maximum.

Allowances related to the ancillary costs of HDRs - examples include relocation costs to undertake an HDR, HDR thesis printing and academic publication costs, and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) costs for international students and their dependants.
For part-time students, the RTP stipend rate is 50% of the full-time rate offered by the university.
The base and maximum stipend rates advised each year apply to all RTP stipend payments made in the relevant year, not just to new recipients.
A student's period of support is increased by the length of an approved RTP scholarship suspension or additional paid personal, parental, partner or family and domestic violence leave.
eligibility: To be eligible (for an RTP fees offset, stipend or allowance) you must be a domestic or international student enrolled in an accredited research doctorate or research masters degree (a higher degree by research) at an eligible Australian university.
At least two-thirds of your time must be spent on research.
Part-time students are eligible for an RTP scholarship.
Students who have undertaken a previous higher degree by research are eligible to apply regardless of their previous enrolment circumstances.
requirements: Meet the eligibility criteria specified in the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025.

Universities must provide a selected student a stipend rate at least equal to the base full-time RTP stipend rate and no more than the maximum full-time RTP stipend rate (section 18 of the Guidelines).
Universities can apply their own selection criteria, and must clearly distinguish them from the student eligibility criteria specified by the Guidelines.
coverage: Tuition fees offset for the HDR course at an eligible Australian university.
A stipend for general living costs.
Allowances related to the ancillary cost of HDRs: relocation costs, HDR thesis printing and academic publication costs, and OSHC for international students and their dependants.
application_method: Contact your chosen eligible higher education provider (university) directly - RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education.
Apply through the university's own HDR admission and RTP scholarship application process.
You may apply for an RTP scholarship at more than one higher education provider.
official.application_route: Apply directly to your chosen eligible Australian university's postgraduate research office; there is no central application portal and the Department of Education does not accept applications.
official.study_mode: Full-time or part-time (published stipend rates are full-time rates; the part-time rate is 50% of the full-time rate offered)
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction: domestic and international (overseas) students are both eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the RTP supports the training of domestic and overseas students at eligible Australian universities.
official.research_requirement: The course must be a research doctorate or research masters (higher degree by research) with at least two-thirds of time spent on research; individual universities set their own research-proposal requirements.
official.duration: Research doctorate: minimum 3 and maximum 4 years at full-time load (minimum 6 and maximum 8 years part-time); research masters: up to 2 years full-time and up to 4 years part-time.
official.description: The Australian Government provides funding to eligible higher education providers through the RTP to support their training of domestic and overseas students undertaking research doctorate and research masters degrees (higher degrees by research). From 1 January 2017, the RTP replaced the Australian Postgraduate Award (APA), the International Postgraduate Research Scholarship (IPRS) and the Research Training Scheme (RTS).
official.program_type: Higher Degree by Research scholarship funded through a research block grant

not_confirmed: selection_criteria (university-specific, not published by the Department)
central deadline (none exists - deadlines are set by each university)
verification.notes: Direct fetches of education.gov.au timed out on 2 attempts, so figures and wording were taken from the Department's own published pages as returned by the search index (RTP page snapshots dated 2025-12-09 and 2026-07-22; student FAQ updated 2026-03-11). Confidence marked low per protocol for unreachable pages, but the 2026 stipend rates (base $34,315, max $53,608) and 2027 rates ($35,550 / $55,537) were consistent across snapshots of the official page.

applicant_utility.summary: The RTP is not one scholarship with one deadline - it is a block grant the Australian Government gives universities, and each university runs its own competitive rounds for PhD and research master's places. A full package pairs a tuition-fee offset with a living stipend (2026 full-time rates run from a base of A$34,315 up to A$53,608 a year, half that for part-time study) plus allowances for relocation, thesis printing and, for international students, Overseas Student Health Cover. Because there is no central portal, your real deadline is the one set by your target university's graduate research school, and most offers hinge on securing a supportive supervisor before you apply.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants with a strong, supervisor-aligned research proposal for an accredited PhD or research master's at an Australian university - domestic and international students alike.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist 2-4 eligible universities and confirm with each graduate research office that they run RTP rounds and what their deadlines are.
Contact prospective supervisors before applying - most RTP offers depend on a supervisor agreeing to support you.
Draft a research proposal clearly aligned to the supervisor's current work.
Prepare transcripts, CV, referees and English or medium-of-instruction evidence to each university's own specifications, not a generic pack.
International applicants: confirm whether the university's RTP allowance covers OSHC and budget accordingly.
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for a central deadline that does not exist and missing university-specific cut-offs.
Applying without a secured or willing supervisor.
A strong academic record paired with a proposal that matches no funded project at the university.
Applying to only one university when its RTP budget is oversubscribed.
Assuming the published full-time rate applies to a part-time offer - it is 50% of the full-time rate.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The base stipend sits below average full-time earnings in Australia; visa charges, OSHC (unless an RTP allowance covers it), relocation beyond any allowance, and city rents - especially Sydney and Melbourne - generally push total uncovered costs well beyond A$34,315 a year.
document_audit: Each university defines its own document set, English test policy and medium-of-instruction rules - the Department publishes none, so work from the specific RTP policy page of each target university.
Only degrees where at least two-thirds of time is research qualify, so coursework-heavy and professional doctorates are not eligible.
Prior HDR study does not disqualify you under the Guidelines, but universities may still apply their own restrictions - check before investing in an application.
alerts: Stipend rates reset every 1 January and the following year's rates are announced by 1 October - the 2027 rates (base A$35,550, max A$55,537) are already published, so 2027-start offers will use them.
Applying at more than one university is explicitly allowed - use it to hedge against oversubscribed rounds.
The Department's FAQ for university administrators addresses a 10 per cent limit on overseas students, so confirm how many international RTP places your target university actually funds.
Recipients must acknowledge support as an 'Australian Government Research Training Program Scholarship' with the Department's DOI in publications.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: University-first: HDR admission and the RTP scholarship are usually assessed together by the graduate research school, typically after a prospective supervisor has backed the application.
